body:
## What

The digits after the decimal point were skipped by `skip_digits()`: 16 compare-and-branch steps in a row, about 3.5 instructions per
digit and an exit branch that is mispredicted when the lengths vary. On x86 with SSE2, the fraction is now skipped by
`skip_fraction_digits()`: 16 bytes are compared at once and the end of the run is taken from the bit mask, about a third of the
instructions for a fraction of 12 digits. The last bytes of the input are skipped one at a time as before. Without SSE2 (AArch64, other targets,
`JSON_NO_SIMD`) `skip_fraction_digits()` is `skip_digits()`: nothing changes there. Integer digits keep `skip_digits()`
(their exit is predictable; an earlier try with word arithmetic for integers made `citm_catalog` 6 % slower).

**GCC-specific part:** GCC unrolls the scalar loop over the last bytes in every inlined copy (`number()` is inlined into the parse loop at several places),
which made the parse loop 4 KiB larger (31,980 -> 35,926 bytes) and files with few fractions 1-4 % slower with more instructions. For GCC
that loop is out of line (`skip_digits_tail()`, +167 bytes instead of +4 KiB); Clang is faster with it inline (an out-of-line tail costs it 5 % on
`instruments`). It is the only compiler-specific `#if` of the change.

## Performance

`json_document::parse()`, A/B in one binary (this branch against `origin/develop`), 6 code layouts, 20 pairs each, x86-64 Haswell, time after / before.
AArch64 is not affected (same code).

| row | GCC 16.2 | Clang 23 |
|---|---|---|
| **numbers.json** (10,001 floats) | **0.717** | **0.683** |
| **canada.json** | **0.775** | **0.783** |
| **mesh.json** | **0.909** | **0.878** |
| **marine_ik.json** | **0.919** | **0.927** |
| **mesh.pretty.json** | **0.914** | **0.945** |
| tree-pretty / instruments | 1.002 / 0.993 | 0.990 / 1.017 |
| gsoc-2018 / twitter | 0.996 / 1.011 | 0.999 / 1.003 |
| prices (20,000 objects with two-decimal prices) | 0.998 | 1.004 |
| fixed6 (60,000 pairs with six decimals) | 1.064 (3) | 0.993 |
| citm_catalog | **1.078** (4) | 0.996 |

(3) Spread 0.99-1.33: one layout of a loaded run; callgrind says -9 % instructions, -19 % branches, -15 % mispredicts for this row.
(4) Stable over the layouts (1.06-1.09) but the instruction count is +0.3 % and mispredicts -11 %: a code-placement effect of GCC on this file. In earlier runs of
the same code on a slightly different base this row was 1.000-1.05, and the same file moved by +-7 % between builds of unrelated variants.
Please weigh it: if you consider a +8 % on one guard row on GCC unacceptable, the other rows show that the idea works and the GCC part could be limited
further, but I have not found a form without it.

Instruction counts (callgrind, GCC 16.2, per parse): `numbers` 0.68 (branches 0.57, simulated mispredicts 0.03), `canada` 0.75 (mispredicts 0.59);
`prices` 1.00 (mispredicts 0.91). The gain is the instruction count; an earlier variant that kept the instruction count and removed only the
mispredicts gained nothing.

## Tests

`json_view builder`, new test case `fraction digits`: fractions of every length from 0 to 40 digits followed by every kind of byte that ends a number
or lies next to the digits in ASCII (`, ] } / : . e E + - x` space, newline, tab, `"`, `0`, `9`), as a root value, in arrays, in objects, and cut in
every place near the end of the text (the length of the number token is what `value_of()` compares with `json::parse()`), for all option combinations and
with and without a terminating NUL. Checked against a deliberate off-by-one at the 16th byte (1,401 assertions fail).

Run locally: all `unit-json_view*.cpp` with clang++ `-std=c++11` on arm64; the builder test on x86-64 with Apple clang (Rosetta), g++ 16 and Clang 23 on Linux
(the compiler-specific tail is only compiled there); `make amalgamate` run. The full CI matrix has not run; MSVC (`_mm_cmplt_epi8` etc. are in
`<emmintrin.h>`, the same header the other SSE2 code uses) and 32-bit x86 are untested.

## Breaking API

No breaking changes. Internal scan function only; the same values and the same errors (tests above); no change to the ABI.

title: json_view: skip the digits of a fraction 16 bytes at a time (SSE2)
